title: Rav Sama son of Rav Ashi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Ketubot 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.33b.1) he raised a difficulty against Rav Ashi: “Is there no difference for you?” etc. In [Menachot 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.25a.9) it reads Rav Sima.

In [Bava Kamma 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.18a.19) and [Zevachim 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.19b.15) and [24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.24a.16) he raised difficulties against Ravina.

In Avodah Zarah 3b (compare [Avodah Zarah 50b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.50b.11)) Rav Sama son of Rav Ashi raised a difficulty against Ravina bar Yirmeyah (in Dikdukei Soferim the reading is “against Ravina,” and the words “bar Yirmeyah” are deleted; but in the Pesaro, Venice and Cracow printings the reading is Rav Sama son of Rav Iti; Hyman prefers this reading; he is the son of Rav Assi, who lived in Rav Ashi’s days and, Hyman says, is always mentioned in the old printings as Rav Iti, as explained in his entry).

In [Ketubot 69a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.69a.13) they said that Ravina collected for Rav Ashi’s daughter from his son Rav Sama, and [Rashi explains](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Ketubot.69a.13.1) that Rav Sama died in the lifetime of Rav Ashi his father; but from Tosafot Rid it is implied that he died later. So too the [Ritva](https://www.sefaria.org/Ritva_on_Ketubot.69a.5) there raised a difficulty against Rashi, and Hyman understands the [Penei Yehoshua](https://www.sefaria.org/Penei_Yehoshua_on_Ketubot.69a.6) as proposing a scribal error in Rashi and reading Rashi to mean that Sama died after Ravina. Hyman identifies this Ravina as the later Ravina, for Ravina, Rav Ashi’s colleague, died before Rav Ashi, as explained in his entry.[^3]

notes.text: Supplied Avodah Zarah3b remains; saved Davidson50b actually contains Sama son of Ashi addressing Ravina bar Yirmeyah, so the matching locus is disclosed alongside it. Hyman’s preferred Iti/Assi and after-Ravina chronology remain his reports and interpretations. Penei Yehoshua is the work meant by פ״י.

The inspected Rashi on Ketubot 69a says Sama died in his father’s lifetime; Tosafot Rid places his death after Rav Ashi, and Ritva objects to Rashi. Penei Yehoshua proposes that Rashi originally read “after him,” referring to Rav Ashi, whereas Hyman prints “after Ravina.” Hyman’s wording is retained and that commentary difference is explicit. The inspected matching dialogue is Avodah Zarah 50b, not the supplied 3b; the Iti/Assi and old-printing claims remain Hyman’s, without new chronology or identity admission.

Ketubot 33b gives both Assi and Ashi as the father’s name. Menachot has Sima son of Idi or Ashi. The exchange with Ravina bar Yirmeyah is at Avodah Zarah 50b. Rashi says that Sama died in his father’s lifetime, which Ritva challenges. Penei Yehoshua proposes “after him,” referring to Rav Ashi. Hyman reports “after Ravina” and separately gives the older-print variant Iti. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2814&lang=en).
